summary: Networking professional with CCNP Enterprise, studying a part-time BSc in Computer Engineering. After 18 months running customer satisfaction for a 1,300-guest hostel, I completed CCNA and CCNP Enterprise training to move into IT. I document everything I build, speak Spanish, English and German, and I am looking for an entry-level role in Berlin in IT support, system administration or network administration.

bullets: Hands-on training in Cisco network design, configuration and troubleshooting. About 70% of the course was lab work: VLANs, OSPF, EIGRP, NAT/PAT, DHCP, ACLs, VLSM and multi-site WAN designs.

Built a redundant enterprise network: two ISP links with BGP, HSRP on the edge and core, port-channels and spanning tree to the access layer, VLANs, DHCP, NAT/PAT and wireless. Tested failover and fixed missing default routes on the core switches.

Built an enterprise branch network: VLSM, router-on-a-stick, central DHCP with relay agents, multi-area OSPF and NAT overload. Fixed missing VLANs, native VLAN mismatches and address gaps that blocked OSPF.
Kept configs and change notes in Git and wrote up every lab on my blog.
Ran customer satisfaction for a 1,300-guest hostel: overbookings, payment problems, noise complaints and maintenance emergencies.
Handled 60–80 escalated cases a week by email and chat in German, English and Spanish, and answered most of them within 4 hours.
Wrote the response templates and the escalation process the team still uses. Repeat guests went up 11% year over year.
